items.statement: India became an independent country on 15th August, 1947.
The Prime Minister and other ministers of the Central Government live in Mumbai.
items.explanation: They live in New Delhi, the capital of India.

items.statement: The Central Government runs the whole country.
There are 9 Union Territories in India.
items.explanation: There are 8 Union Territories in India.

items.statement: Bal Gangadhar Tilak is also known as 'Iron Man of India'.
Mahatma Gandhi is called the 'Father of Nation'.
Mahatma Gandhi studied law in America.
The slogan 'Jai Hind' was used by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose to encourage Indians.
Vehicles carry people and goods from one place to another.
We must not follow the road safety rules.
Camel is called the 'Ship of the Desert'.
We must not use zebra crossing to cross the road.

items.prompt: How many States and Union Territories are there in India?
What is the law-making body of the Central Government?
Where does the President of India live?
Who looks after the country just like the head of the family?
Who looks after the Union Territories?
Which event was successfully hosted by the city of Delhi in 2023?
Which national leader is also known as the 'Father of the Nation'?
What was Mahatma Gandhi's full name?
What is the name of the women's army unit formed by Subhash Chandra Bose?

items.question: Government
items.answer: A governing body that looks after the welfare and safety of the people. It frames laws.

items.question: Central Government
items.answer: It is the government elected by the people to govern the country.

items.question: State Government
items.answer: It is the government elected by the people to govern the state.

items.question: Union Territories
items.answer: Small parts of India that are directly controlled by the Central Government.

items.question: Transportation
items.answer: It means to carry people and goods from place to place by means of vehicles.

items.question: Subway
items.answer: It is an underground way to cross the road safely.

items.question: Level Crossing
items.answer: It is a place where a railway line and a road cross each other.

items.question: What is a Government?
items.answer: The government is a governing body that looks after the welfare and safety of the people.

items.question: Name any three Union Territories.
What are the responsibilities of a State Government?
items.answer: The State Government looks after education, health, welfare of the people and also maintains law and order.

items.question: What is Mumbai also known for?
items.answer: Mumbai is also known as the entertainment and business capital of India.

items.question: When and where was Mahatma Gandhi born? What did he study in England?
items.answer: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2nd October, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat. He studied law in England.

items.question: Which slogan was given by Lokmanya Tilak to encourage millions of Indians?
items.answer: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."

items.question: Which two slogans were used by Netaji to encourage the Indians?
items.answer: "Jai Hind" and "Give me blood, I will give you freedom."

items.question: What are the common means of transport used in villages?
items.answer: In Indian villages, bullock carts or animal carts are used to carry goods and people.

items.question: Why do people need to be careful on the roads or streets?
items.answer: Because even a bit of carelessness can cost them their life.

items.question: Why do we use means of transport?
items.answer: Means of transport help people to travel from one place to another.

items.question: List the responsibilities of the Government.
answer: Frames laws to run the country smoothly.
Provides services like electricity, water, telephone and communication.
Decides where to build roads, schools, hospitals, stadiums, parks, stations and airports.

items.question: What are the functions of the Central Government?
items.answer: The Central Government is like the head of the family that runs the whole nation. It helps the State Government whenever help is needed.

items.question: Why has India been divided into States and Union Territories?
items.answer: India is a big country, and it was not possible for one government to look after such a big country. Hence, it is divided into States and Union Territories.

items.question: How are Union Territories different from States?
items.answer: Every State has its own government, but Union Territories are under the direct control of the Central Government.

items.question: List (a) any five places of tourist interest in Delhi (b) two government offices located in Delhi.
answer: (a) Red Fort, India Gate, Qutub Minar, Jantar Mantar, Nehru Planetarium
(b) Parliament, Prime Minister's Office

items.question: What are embassies?
items.answer: The governments of other countries have offices in Delhi. These foreign offices are called Embassies or High Commissions.

items.question: List any five tourist spots of Mumbai.
items.answer: Gateway of India, Jehangir Art Gallery, Marine Drive, Taraporewala Aquarium, Essel World.

items.question: Why is New Delhi often referred to as 'Lutyens' Delhi'?
items.answer: The city of Delhi was planned and designed by British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens. Therefore, it is often referred to as 'Lutyens' Delhi'.

items.question: Why is Mumbai called the 'City of Dreams'?
items.answer: People from all over India come to Mumbai for employment or to become actors. It is home to many television and film stars, so Mumbai is called the City of Dreams.

items.question: Describe the climate of Delhi.
items.answer: The climate of Delhi is extreme. It has very hot summers. Hot and dry winds called loo blow from April to June. The winters are very cold, and it rains from July to September.

items.question: Write a short note on the transport system of Mumbai.
answer: Local train networks connect the city very well and it is the best public transport system in Mumbai.
The city also has one of the busiest railway stations in India — the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST).

items.question: What makes Delhi a well-connected city?
answer: Well-developed modern roads, bridges and flyovers have made Delhi a modern and comfortable city to live in.
Delhi Metro provides a fast and cheap means of transport to the people.

items.question: Why do you think Delhi is called a 'Mini India'?
answer: Delhi is famous for job opportunities and education, so people from different states come here.
Many universities in Delhi are great centres of learning and higher education; students from all over the world come to study here.

items.question: Why do you think Bombay High is of great importance?
items.answer: Bombay High is an important place because mineral oil is found here in the seabed. This mineral oil is purified in a refinery.

items.question: What were the two methods used by Mahatma Gandhi to fight against the British?
Write three sentences on Sardar Patel.
items.answer: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was a lawyer by profession. He was a strong and brave leader. He was inspired by Mahatma Gandhi to take part in the struggle for freedom. He is also known as the 'Iron Man of India'.

items.question: Why did Rani Laxmibai fight against the British?
items.answer: Rani Laxmibai fought against the British because she wanted to save her kingdom from the British. She joined the soldiers from Meerut and fought for Jhansi. She, along with other leaders, fought against the British in the Revolt of 1857.

items.question: Great people never give up in spite of difficulties. What do you do when you face difficulties in your studies?
items.answer: When I face difficulties in my studies, I never give up. I try again and again. I take help from my teacher and parents. I practice more and more until I understand well.

items.question: List any five rules for road safety.
answer: Cross the road using the zebra crossing.
Look right, then left, then right again before crossing the road.
Walk on the footpath.
Obey traffic rules and cross the road only when the traffic stops.
If cycling to school, keep to the left; use bylanes to stay safe.

items.question: Write short notes on the following means of transport:
answer: Land: These means of transport move only on land. Example: buses, tractors, cars.
Water: These means of transport move only on water. Example: ships, boats, tankers and steamers.
Air: It is the fastest means of transport. Used to cover long distances in less time. Example: aeroplane, helicopter.
Animal: Animal transport has been a means of transport since ancient times. The camel is used in the desert, ponies and mules are used in hilly areas, and elephants are used in forest areas.

items.question: Why should we use subways?
items.answer: Subways help us reach places quickly without getting stuck in traffic. Subways and foot-over bridges should be used to cross the roads.

items.question: Kanika lives in Mumbai. What kind of clothes do you think she wears in (a) summer (b) winter?
answer: Summer in Mumbai is warm and humid, so Kanika wears light, cotton clothes.
Winters are not very cold but pleasant, so she wears light but warm clothes.

items.question: Mahatma Gandhi was a messenger of peace. What can you learn from him as a leader?
items.answer: I can learn to always speak the truth and be honest. I can solve problems in a peaceful way without fighting. I can be kind and helpful to others and respect everyone equally. I can also learn to stand up for what is right and work hard for the welfare of the people.

items.question: What mode of transportation, regardless of cost, would you choose if you needed to get somewhere far away in the least amount of time? Explain.
items.answer: I would choose an aeroplane or a helicopter to travel to a far-away place in the least amount of time because they are the fastest mode of transport.

items.question: Who looks after our country just like the head of a family?

items.question: In which one of the following cities does the Chief Minister of Uttarakhand live and work?

items.question: Which one of the following cities is the common capital of Punjab and Haryana?

items.question: Which one of the following statements is true about the Union Territories of India?
items.options: (a) There are 8 Union Territories in India.  (b) They are under direct control of the Central Government.  (c) They are not included in any of the 28 states.  (d) All of these

items.question: Water scarcity is a problem for farmers in a region. They go to the ______ to meet the Governor of their State to find a solution.
items.options: (a) Rashtrapati Bhawan  (b) Raj Bhawan  (c) Parliament House  (d) High Court

items.question: The ______ built New Delhi as the Capital of India.
items.options: (a) French  (b) Portuguese  (c) Americans  (d) British

items.question: Which one of the following stadiums is not in Delhi?
items.options: (a) Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium  (b) Indira Gandhi Stadium  (c) Talkatora Stadium  (d) Narendra Modi Stadium

items.question: Which one of the following places of Mumbai is famously known as Queen's Necklace?
items.options: (a) the CST  (b) Malabar Hills  (c) the Elephanta Caves  (d) the Marine Drive

items.question: Which one of the following states is a neighbouring state of Delhi?
items.options: (a) Uttarakhand  (b) Maharashtra  (c) Haryana  (d) Punjab

items.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about New Delhi?
items.options: (a) New Delhi is our national capital.  (b) It is a beautiful city situated along the banks of the River Yamuna.  (c) It was first built by the Pandava Kings.  (d) All of these

items.question: Which one of the following statements is true about Mumbai?
items.options: (a) Mumbai was at one time a group of seven islands.  (b) Mumbai lies on the west coast of India.  (c) Both (a) and (b)  (d) Mumbai is the capital of India.

items.question: You visit Mumbai in the month of May. You experience a ______ climate.
items.options: (a) warm and humid  (b) cold and dry  (c) cool and pleasant  (d) cool and wet

items.question: Mahatma Gandhi was born on ______.
items.options: (a) 2 October 1879  (b) 2 October 1869  (c) 2 October 1969  (d) 2 October 1959

items.question: Mahatma Gandhi used ______ and Ahimsa to fight against the British.
items.options: (a) Satyagraha  (b) non-violence  (c) army  (d) navy

items.question: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was a brave and ______ leader.
items.options: (a) old  (b) weak  (c) strong  (d) none of these

items.question: Sardar Patel was a ______ by profession.
items.options: (a) lawyer  (b) doctor  (c) military man  (d) teacher

items.question: ______ was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress.
items.options: (a) Lakshmi Bai  (b) Indira Gandhi  (c) Sarojini Naidu  (d) Jhalkari Bai

items.question: Rani Lakshmi Bai was the Queen of ______.
items.options: (a) Meerut  (b) Jhansi  (c) Uttar Pradesh  (d) Delhi

items.question: The choice of transport depends on ______.
items.options: (a) the distance to be travelled  (b) the money we have  (c) time available  (d) all of these

items.question: Which one of the following means of transport is used to send huge amounts of grain from one country to another?
items.options: (a) Car  (b) Ship  (c) Helicopter  (d) Bullock Cart

items.question: What are the two kinds of land transport?
items.options: (a) camels and ponies  (b) aeroplanes and helicopters  (c) cars and trains  (d) ships and yachts

items.question: Which one of the following options is true about level crossing?
items.options: (a) It is a place where a railway line and a road cross each other.  (b) We should not cross a railway track when the gates are down.  (c) Level crossings can be dangerous.  (d) All of these

items.question: What will you use to move big logs of wood in thick forests?
items.options: (a) elephants  (b) camels  (c) ponies  (d) bullock carts
